seo.title: Best Vegan Restaurants in Berlin (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the 12 best vegan restaurants in Berlin for 2026, from upscale zero-waste dining to classic vegan döner. Find top picks for every budget and experience.

hero.subtitle: Berlin's vegan food scene is a global leader, offering an incredible diversity of innovative, ethical, and delicious plant-based dining experiences across all cuisines and budgets.

picks.name: Frea
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Frea is Berlin's pioneering zero-waste vegan restaurant, offering a rotating seasonal tasting menu crafted from regionally sourced, organic ingredients. Their commitment to sustainability extends to every detail, including composting all food scraps and returning them to their partner farm. The atmosphere is elegant yet relaxed, perfect for a special occasion.
picks.whatToOrder: The daily changing 5-course tasting menu is the only option, ensuring you experience their freshest, most innovative creations.
picks.insiderTip: Book well in advance, especially for weekend evenings, as their tables fill up quickly due to high demand and limited seating.
picks.redditQuote: "Frea blew my mind. Zero waste, incredible flavors, and I loved knowing everything was sourced locally. Definitely worth the splurge for a unique meal in Berlin."

picks.name: Kopps
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Kopps offers refined vegan German and European cuisine in a sleek, inviting setting. They focus on seasonal, organic ingredients, transforming traditional dishes into sophisticated plant-based creations. It's an excellent choice for those seeking a more upscale dining experience without the formality of fine dining.
picks.whatToOrder: Their seasonal takes on classic German dishes like Königsberger Klopse or innovative risotto variations are always a hit.
picks.insiderTip: They offer a fantastic brunch buffet on weekends, which is a great way to sample a wide variety of their delicious offerings at a fixed price.
picks.redditQuote: "Kopps is consistently excellent. The food is so thoughtfully prepared, and you can really taste the quality of the ingredients. Great for a nice dinner out."

picks.name: Viasko
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Viasko is a beloved Kreuzberg institution, known for its hearty vegan comfort food and relaxed pub atmosphere. They offer a diverse menu ranging from traditional German dishes like Schnitzel and goulash to burgers and salads, all completely plant-based. It's a cozy spot perfect for a casual dinner with friends.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Schnitzel' with potato salad or their legendary vegan Goulash are must-tries for a taste of German comfort.
picks.insiderTip: Visit on a Sunday for their popular all-you-can-eat vegan brunch buffet, featuring a huge spread of sweet and savory options.
picks.redditQuote: "Viasko is my go-to for proper German comfort food without the meat. Their Schnitzel is surprisingly good, and the vibe is super chill."

picks.name: Vöner
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Vöner is a Berlin original, famous for perfecting the vegan döner kebab. This bustling spot offers delicious, generously portioned plant-based versions of the city's iconic street food, along with other quick bites like burgers and fries. It's the ultimate stop for a satisfying and affordable meal.
picks.whatToOrder: The classic 'Vöner Teller' (döner plate) or a 'Vöner im Brot' (döner in bread) with all the fixings.
picks.insiderTip: Expect a queue during peak hours, especially late evenings. It moves fast, but be prepared for a short wait.
picks.redditQuote: "You haven't truly experienced Berlin vegan food until you've had a Vöner. It hits different after a night out, so much flavor and super cheap."

picks.name: Brammibal's Donuts
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Brammibal's Donuts revolutionized Berlin's sweet scene with their incredible all-vegan donuts. With multiple locations, this vibrant bakery offers an imaginative array of flavors, from classic glazed to unique seasonal creations. It's perfect for a sweet treat, breakfast, or coffee break.
picks.whatToOrder: Try a classic like the salted caramel or a seasonal special like Pistachio Lemon. Don't forget their excellent coffee.
picks.insiderTip: Go early for the best selection, especially on weekends, as popular flavors often sell out by afternoon.
picks.redditQuote: "Brammibal's donuts are pure magic. You'd never know they're vegan. I always grab a half dozen when I'm in Berlin."

picks.name: Alaska Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Alaska Bar brings the vibrant flavors of vegan Spanish tapas to Berlin. This cozy, dimly lit bar in Neukölln offers a fantastic selection of small plates, perfect for sharing, alongside creative cocktails and natural wines. It's an ideal spot for a lively evening with friends or a romantic date.
picks.whatToOrder: The Patatas Bravas, 'Chorizo' al Vino, and a selection of their seasonal vegetable tapas are highly recommended.
picks.insiderTip: They don't take reservations, so arrive early on weekends or be prepared for a short wait for a table.
picks.redditQuote: "Alaska Bar has the best vegan tapas in Berlin, hands down. Everything is so flavorful, and the cocktails are amazing. It gets busy, but it's worth it."

picks.name: Lia's Kitchen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Lia's Kitchen is a go-to for delicious and satisfying vegan burgers in Prenzlauer Berg. They serve up generously sized burgers with creative toppings, crispy fries, and fresh salads in a casual, friendly setting. It's perfect for a quick, tasty, and guilt-free meal.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Lia's Burger' with their signature sauces and a side of sweet potato fries.
picks.insiderTip: Consider ordering online for pickup during lunch or dinner rush to skip potential waits for a table or your order.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously good vegan burgers at Lia's Kitchen. The patties are flavorful, and they have so many topping options. My favorite burger joint in Berlin."

picks.name: Sfizy Veg
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sfizy Veg is Berlin's first 100% vegan pizzeria, offering a fantastic array of classic and creative pizzas made with high-quality plant-based cheeses and toppings. Located in the heart of Neukölln, it's a cozy spot perfect for satisfying your pizza cravings in an animal-friendly way.
picks.whatToOrder: Try the 'Pizza Diavola' for a spicy kick or the 'Pizza Funghi' for a classic mushroom option. They also have great calzones.
picks.insiderTip: They offer gluten-free crust options, making it accessible for those with dietary restrictions.
picks.redditQuote: "Sfizy Veg makes me forget about dairy cheese. Their pizzas are legit, perfectly crispy crusts and loaded with flavor. A must for vegan pizza lovers."

picks.name: Chaostheorie
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Chaostheorie is a unique vegan bar and eatery in Prenzlauer Berg, offering a relaxed atmosphere, a great selection of drinks, and delicious plant-based bar food. It's a popular spot for both food and drinks, perfect for a casual evening out with friends.
picks.whatToOrder: Their vegan 'Currywurst' with fries is a fantastic local staple, or try one of their hearty burgers.
picks.insiderTip: They have a creative cocktail menu – ask the bartender for their recommendations based on your preferences.
picks.redditQuote: "Chaostheorie is just a cool spot. Good drinks, good vegan grub, and a very laid-back vibe. Perfect for a casual hang out."

picks.name: Mom's Creation
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mom's Creation offers authentic and flavorful vegan Vietnamese cuisine in a warm, inviting setting. Their menu features a wide range of traditional dishes, from aromatic pho to crispy spring rolls and vibrant curries, all prepared with fresh ingredients and careful attention to flavor.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Pho Chay' (vegan pho) is wonderfully comforting, or try the 'Bun Cha Gio' (vermicelli salad with spring rolls).
picks.insiderTip: Their lunch specials offer excellent value, providing a main dish and often a small starter for a reduced price.
picks.redditQuote: "I could eat at Mom's Creation every day. The pho is so rich and flavorful, and everything tastes incredibly fresh. A hidden gem for vegan Vietnamese."

picks.name: Rawtastic
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Rawtastic is Berlin's dedicated raw vegan restaurant, offering a menu packed with nutrient-dense, enzyme-rich dishes prepared without cooking above 42°C. From vibrant salads and creative main courses to indulgent desserts, it's a paradise for health-conscious diners looking for fresh, living foods.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Zucchini Pasta' or the 'Raw Lasagna' are popular choices, and definitely save room for their delicious raw cheesecakes.
picks.insiderTip: The portion sizes are generous, but everything is light, so don't be afraid to try a starter and a main.
picks.redditQuote: "Rawtastic is amazing if you're into raw vegan. The food is so fresh and vibrant, and the desserts are surprisingly decadent. Feel so good after eating there."

picks.name: Vincent Vegan
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Vincent Vegan brings classic American-style fast food to the plant-based world with their delicious burgers, hot dogs, and fries. Found in several locations including the East Side Mall, it's a quick and easy option for satisfying your fast-food cravings without compromise.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Big V Burger' and a side of crispy fries with their special sauce are a classic combo.
picks.insiderTip: Look for their food trucks at various festivals and events around the city for a convenient grab-and-go meal.
picks.redditQuote: "Sometimes you just need a good vegan burger and fries, and Vincent Vegan nails it every time. Reliable and satisfying fast food."

faq.question: Is Berlin a good city for vegans?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Berlin is widely considered one of the best, if not the best, vegan cities in the world. It boasts an incredibly diverse and extensive vegan scene, with hundreds of restaurants, cafes, bakeries, and even supermarkets dedicated to plant-based food. You'll find options ranging from upscale fine dining to casual street food, catering to every taste and budget.

faq.question: Are vegan restaurants in Berlin expensive?
faq.answer: The cost of vegan restaurants in Berlin varies widely, just like any other cuisine. You can find very affordable options, such as döner kebabs from Vöner (€8-12) or fast-casual burgers (€10-15). There are also mid-range restaurants (€15-30) and high-end fine dining experiences like Frea (€70-100+). There's truly something for every budget.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for vegan restaurants in Berlin?
faq.answer: For popular or upscale vegan restaurants, especially on weekend evenings, making a reservation is highly recommended. Places like Frea or Kopps often book out weeks in advance. For more casual spots or during weekdays, you might be fine walking in, but a quick call ahead or checking their website is always a good idea, particularly for larger groups.

faq.question: What kind of vegan food can I expect in Berlin?
faq.answer: Berlin's vegan food scene is incredibly diverse. You can expect innovative modern European cuisine, traditional German comfort food reimagined, excellent Asian (Vietnamese, Thai, Japanese), Italian (pizza, pasta), Spanish tapas, American-style burgers, healthy raw vegan options, and plenty of street food like döner and currywurst. Dessert options, especially vegan donuts and cakes, are also plentiful and exceptional.

faq.question: Are there vegan-friendly hotels or grocery stores in Berlin?
faq.answer: Yes, Berlin is very vegan-friendly across the board. Many hotels offer vegan breakfast options upon request, and some even cater specifically to vegan travelers. For groceries, you'll find numerous dedicated vegan supermarkets like Veganz, as well as a wide selection of vegan products in conventional supermarkets (Lidl, Rewe, Edeka) and organic stores (Bio Company, Denn's Biomarkt).

faq.question: What are some must-try vegan dishes unique to Berlin?
faq.answer: Beyond classic vegan options, Berlin has popularized a few unique plant-based staples. You absolutely must try a 'Vöner' (vegan döner kebab), a vegan 'Currywurst', and explore the incredible variety of vegan donuts from places like Brammibal's. Many restaurants also offer veganized versions of traditional German dishes like 'Schnitzel' or 'Königsberger Klopse'.

methodology: Our selection of Berlin's best vegan restaurants is based on extensive research, local expert recommendations, and an analysis of diner reviews across multiple platforms. We prioritize establishments known for their innovative menus, high-quality ingredients, consistent service, and unique dining experiences, ensuring a diverse representation of cuisines and price points.
